sentences.text: Erpetosuchus belongs to the family Erpetosuchidae and is classified within the unranked family Paracrocodylomorpha.
E. T. Newton first described Erpetosuchus in 1894 based on four specimens from the latest Carnian Lossiemouth Sandstone Formation in northeastern Scotland.
American paleontologist Paul E. Olsen discovered a partial skull in Connecticut in 1995, marking the first record of the genus found outside Scotland.
This Connecticut specimen was recovered from the New Haven Formation, which dates to the Norian age.
Originally assigned to Thecodontia, this classification is now considered invalid.
An analysis by Olsen et al. in 2000 suggested Erpetosuchus granti is the sister-taxon to Crocodylomorpha.
This animal lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Late Triassic period, specifically in the Norian stage.
It is debated whether Erpetosuchus is closely related to Crocodylomorpha, as some analyses suggest an unresolved relationship at the base of Archosauria instead.
